newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-PARK STRIKESOUT 11 AS DODGERS BEAT BRAVES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-PARK STRIKESOUT 11 AS DODGERS BEAT BRAVES.

text.p: Chan Ho Park struck out 11 in 6-1/3 innings for his third straight win and snapped a tie with a fourth-inning single as the Los Angeles Dodgers defeated the Atlanta Braves, 8-3 on Sunday.
Park (8-5) allowed three runs and six hits before departing in the seventh. He walked just two.
"It was hot and humid," Park said. "It felt just like Korea. It helped that I had a good Korean meal last night -- soup and rice. Atlanta has good Korean food."
Raul Mondesi hit a two-run homer and scored twice for the Dodgers, who are 12-5 in July.
Smoltz (8-9) already has lost more games than he did all of last season, when he went 24-8.

In Chicago, Larry Walker went 3-for-5 with two homers and four RBI and Vinny Castilla also homered twice as the Colorado Rockies pounded their way out of an eight-game losing streak with a 9-5 victory over the Chicago Cubs.
Walker, who went 0-for-9 in Saturday's doubleheader loss, rebounded today to get his season batting average back up to .395.

In Montreal, Darryl Kile threw a four-hitter for his fourth shutout of the season and Luis Gonzalez homered twice and had six RBI as the Houston Astros cruised to a 9-0 victory over the Montreal Expos.
Kile (13-3) was 2-for-3 and scored a run. He also dropped his ERA to 1.99 and matched Greg Maddux and Denny Neagle of the Atlanta Braves for the National League lead in wins.
Gonzalez had three of Houston's eight hits and went 9-for-11 in the three-game series.

In New York, Todd Hundley homered from both sides of the plate for the fifth time in his career as part of a 4-for-4, five-RBI effort, and Dave Mlicki won for the first time in a month as the New York Mets pounded the Cincinnati Reds, 10-1.
Hundley also had an RBI double in the first and reached on an infield single in the fifth for his fifth career four-hit game.
"It wasn't a bad day," he said. "They don't come around too often, you have to take advantage of it. I was fortunate to hit with men in scoring position."
Bernard Gilkey added three hits, including his third homer in four games, for New York, which has won four straight.

In Philadelphia, Garrett Stephenson allowed one run in 6-2/3 innings, and Midre Cummings haunted his former team with the go-ahead triple in the fifth as the Philadelphia Phillies recorded a 4-1 victory over the Pittsburgh Pirates.
Stephenson (4-4) allowed seven hits and walked two with six strikeouts for Philadelphia, which has won four of its last six games,.

"I feel great," Stephenson said. "I've noticed improvement in my game and I seem to be getting more and more confident out there. They kept me in some big situations and that helped. I thought my off-speed stuff really helped me today."
Stephenson, Curt Schilling and Mark Leiter have combined for 19 of Philadelphia's 29 victories.

In St Louis, Kirk Rueter allowed six hits over seven innings and Barry Bonds triggered an offensive explosion with a first-inning homer -- his 24th -- to lead the San Francisco Giants a 9-2 victory over the St. Louis Cardinals
Rueter (7-4) won his second straight start, both on the road. The only run he allowed came on a double-play grounder in the fourth inning.
Bonds' homer off starter Alan Benes (9-8) gave the Giants the lead for good and set the tone. San Francisco collected 13 hits.
At Florida, Andy Ashby and two relievers combined on a six-hitter and Chris Gomez snapped a seventh-inning tie with a two-run triple as the San Diego Padres blanked the Florida Marlins, 3-0.
Ashby (6-6) scattered four hits and four walks and struck out six over seven innings to win his third straight road start. He has alternated wins and losses in his last eight outings.
